dialect.guess: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) or Micro Focus COBOL — JMA ORCA project (Japanese Medical Association)
evidence: ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED / ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC
No EXEC SQL / EXEC CICS — pure file-based batch

purpose.summary: Batch program that creates monthly insurance-claim detail files for 'Rousai' (workers' accident) and 'Jibaiseki' (compulsory automobile liability) insurance categories. It reads indexed RECE41/RECE44/RECE45 claim files, processes and filters records (including cancellation handling), and writes output to RECE441/RECE451 indexed files, with error logging to RECEERR. It is part of the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt (claims) software system.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical insurance claims (Japanese national health insurance billing)

notable_features: Japanese EUC or Shift-JIS encoded comments (decoded as latin-1, hence garbled)
COPY ... REPLACING with double-slash delimiters (OpenCOBOL/GnuCOBOL style)
Multiple FD entries sharing the same physical file via ASSIGN aliases (RECE4441-FILE and RECE441-FILE both assign RECE441PARA)
LINKAGE SECTION with COMMAND-PARAM for parameter passing
Job management sub-program calls (ORCSJOB, ORCSJOBKANRI pattern)
No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS — pure sequential/indexed file processing
Full-width Japanese numeral tables (TBL-TUKI-AREA, TBL-DAY-AREA) for date display conversion
verdict.notes: Comments are in Japanese (EUC-JP or Shift-JIS) but the file was decoded as latin-1, producing mojibake. The program is clearly part of the well-known JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system. COPY statements reference external copybooks (.INC files) that are not shown, so full data layout cannot be verified, but all structural indicators confirm genuine production COBOL.
